question: What is the LCM of 3.6, 1.8 and 0.144?
solution:
**Given data:**

Number = 3.6, 1.8, and 0.144

**Calculation:**

Digit with highest digits after decimal = 0.144 

⇒ 3 digits after decimal i.e., n = 3 = 10³ 

⇒ 3.6 × 103 = 3600

⇒ 1.8 × 103 = 1800

⇒ 0.144 × 103 = 144

Finding the LCM of (3600, 1800, 144) = 3600

LCM = {3600over 10³}= 3.6

∴ **The LCM of the given numbers is 3.6.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**The LCM of 3.6, 1.8 and 0.144

LCM of (3.6, 1.8, 0.144)

⇒ LCM of (3600/1000, 1800/1000, 144/1000)

⇒ LCM of (3600/1000, 1800/1000, 144/1000) = (LCM of (3600, 1800, 144))/(HCF of (1000, 1000, 1000))

⇒ 3600/1000 = 3.6

∴ The LCM of the given numbers is 3.6.
